<details>
This .SRCINFO file is standard AUR packaging metadata (auto-generated from a PKGBUILD) with no executable content. It declares a binary package "mesh-client-bin" that fetches prebuilt .deb files from the project's own upstream GitHub releases: https://github.com/Colorado-Mesh/mesh-client/releases/download/v6.1.0/. The download destinations are the project's official release host (GitHub), not an unrelated or untrusted source.

Security is further strengthened by the presence of pinned SHA256 checksums for both x86_64 and aarch64 builds, which verify file integrity against tampering. There is no obfuscation, no base64/eval chains, no curl|bash style piped execution, and no data exfiltration or backdoor mechanisms. The dependencies listed (at-spi2-core, gtk3, libnotify, libsecret, nss, etc.) are all standard GUI/Electron runtime libraries consistent with the package's stated purpose as an Electron desktop client.

The only minor hygiene note is that it downloads .deb packages from GitHub rather than building from source, but this is a common and acceptable AUR pattern for binary packages, and the checksums mitigate supply-chain risk. No genuinely malicious behavior is present.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard, well-formed package for a prebuilt binary Electron application (mesh-client-bin). Every operation follows ordinary AUR packaging practices for -bin packages:

1. **Sources**: Downloads official DEB binaries from the project's own upstream GitHub releases (`github.com/Colorado-Mesh/mesh-client/releases/download/v${pkgver}/...`) over HTTPS, one per architecture (x86_64, aarch64). URLs are pinned to a specific version tag.

2. **prepare()**: Extracts the DEB's `data.tar.*` with `bsdtar`, then uses `sed -i` to fix up the upstream-provided desktop file (correcting the Exec line and adding categories). This only modifies a single application-owned `.desktop` file.

3. **package()**: Installs the Electron app from its self-contained `/opt/Mesh-client` tree into `usr/lib`, creates a `/usr/bin` wrapper symlink, sets the expected SUID bit on Electron's `chrome-sandbox` helper (required for the app to start), and installs the desktop file and icons.

No evidence of malicious behavior: no downloads from unrelated hosts, no `curl|bash`-style code execution, no base64/hex obfuscation, no `eval`, no exfiltration, and no tampering with files outside the application's own scope. The dependencies (gtk3, libnotify, nss, etc.) are typical for an Electron app. This is legitimate supply-chain behavior — packaging upstream's own released binaries with provided SHA256 checksums.
</details>

Standard prebuilt Electron binary package; no malicious activity found.

</security_assessment>
